posts.author: vicebeachcam
posts.title: I went through the Extended Look and listed every location that is actually named on screen
posts.body:
Rules I set for myself: it counts if a sign, a marker, or the narration names it. No guessing from architecture.

1. Vice City, and inside it Ocean Beach, Little Cuba, the Stockyard, Crosstown, the VC Port.
2. Leonida Keys.
3. Grassrivers.
4. Port Gellhorn.
5. Ambrosia, with the Allied Crystal refinery.
6. Mount Kalaga National Park.

Road signage also gives Vice-Dale County and Kelly County, which are counties and not regions. Everything else people are posting is inference. Good inference in some cases, but inference.

posts.author: mapnerd_leonida
posts.title: Running the actual numbers on the map size claim
posts.body:
Rockstar said Vice City is roughly twice Los Santos, and the full map is about three times RDR2's. People are treating those as the same claim and they are not.

RDR2's playable area is commonly put around 75 square km. Three times that is somewhere near 225. GTA V's whole map including the countryside is usually estimated around 75 to 80 as well, with Los Santos proper being a fraction of it.

So the city being double Los Santos does not mean the city is huge relative to the state. It means the state is enormous and the city is a dense chunk of it. Those are very different games to play.

Keys are south, obviously. Mount Kalaga is described as being on the state's northern border. Vice City is the anchor. That leaves Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn and Ambrosia to place, and the descriptions give us wetlands, a forgotten coast, and inland industrial.

So Grassrivers is probably west or inland of the city, Port Gellhorn is coastal but not the same coast, and Ambrosia is inland. That is my read. Poke holes in it.

posts.author: vicebeachcam
posts.title: The supporting cast bios read like a mission structure if you line them up

Boobie Ike owns real estate, a club and a studio. Dre'Quan runs the label inside that studio and has signed the Real Dimez. Raul Bautista robs banks and recruits people willing to take risks. Cal Hampton sits at home believing things.

That is not four characters. That is four mission strands: property and legitimate business, music and clout, high risk robbery, and whatever Cal accidentally uncovers.

Rockstar has released character bios before but I do not think they have ever mapped this cleanly onto what you will actually be doing.

posts.author: preloadwatch
posts.title: Preorder breakdown, what each version actually gets you
posts.body:
Putting this in one place because I keep answering it in comments.

Standard, 79.99. Full campaign, nothing else.

Ultimate, 99.99. Adds a set of vehicles, weapons and cosmetics, plus several businesses with side missions layered through the story. Content unlocks as you progress rather than all at once.

Vintage Vice City Pack. Comes with any preorder of either edition, digital before November 20 or physical while stocks last.

GTA plus free month. Digital preorders through the PlayStation or Microsoft stores only.

Have I missed anything?

Three months out and this is the boring advice nobody takes until the week of launch.

posts.author: mapnerd_leonida
posts.title: The six regions are not equal in size and everyone is treating them as though they are
posts.body:
Vice City is described as roughly twice Los Santos. The other five regions share whatever is left of a state that is about triple RDR2's area.

That does not divide into five equal pieces. The Keys are a chain, which is long and narrow. A national park on a state border is probably large. A forgotten coast is probably a strip. Ambrosia is agricultural, which in real life means enormous and mostly empty.

So the useful mental model is not six regions, it is one dense city and five very differently shaped spaces around it. Every adjacency map I have seen draws them as six similar blobs and that is almost certainly wrong.

posts.author: keysrunner_88
posts.title: Six named regions is more than any GTA has had and that number is doing work
posts.body:
III had one city. Vice City had one city and two islands. San Andreas had three cities and the countryside between them, which is the closest comparison. IV had one city. V had a city and a county.

This has six named regions, each with its own official description and its own character. That is a structural decision, not a marketing one. Naming a region commits you to making it feel different from the others, and six is a lot of different to commit to.

San Andreas is the only precedent and that game is twenty two years old.

posts.author: vicebeachcam
posts.title: Trailer view records are a bad metric and this forum keeps quoting them as evidence
posts.body:
Trailer 1 took the twenty four hour record. Trailer 2 took it again with a much bigger number across all platforms. The Extended Look did thirty one million on a streaming service in four days and topped their chart in most countries.

All of that is true and none of it tells you anything about the game. View counts measure anticipation, distribution and platform mechanics. They are a measure of how well a marketing department did, not of what shipped.

I am not being sour. I am saying that when someone uses a view count as an argument in a thread about whether the game will be good, that is not an argument.

posts.author: keysrunner_88
posts.title: What the 2002 Vice City got right that nothing since has matched
posts.body:
Not nostalgia for its own sake. Trying to name the actual thing.

It was small. You could hold the whole map in your head after a week, and that meant every location had an identity rather than a coordinate. The Malibu Club was not a building, it was the Malibu Club. Print Works was a place you owned and thought about.

Every map since has been bigger and none of them has been as memorable, because memorability is not a function of size. A modern Vice City that is twice the size of Los Santos has to solve that problem, and I have no idea whether they can.

posts.author: sixstarsplz
posts.title: Wanted levels explained for people who have never played one of these
posts.body:
Writing this for the newcomers group because I get asked and because I think about it constantly.

Old system: you do a crime, stars appear immediately, more stars means more police and worse police. You escape by getting away and staying out of sight until a timer runs down.

New system as described: a crime has to be seen and reported before police respond properly. What the witness saw becomes a description covering your face, your clothes and your vehicle. Hollow stars mean they are looking but do not know who they are looking for. You escape by breaking the description, not just by breaking away.

Six stars instead of five, so the top end goes higher. That is the whole thing.

posts.author: keysrunner_88
posts.title: The 2002 radio lineup was seven stations and every single one had a job
posts.body:
Going through this because people keep saying they want the old soundtrack back and I think they want something more specific than that.

V-Rock was the loud one. Flash FM was the pop one. Wave 103 was the cold synth one for driving at night. Fever 105 was the smooth one. Emotion 98.3 was the sad one for when the mission went badly. Radio Espantoso was the one that made the city feel like it belonged to someone other than you. VCPR was the one you left on because it was funnier than the driving.

Seven stations, seven distinct moods, and you could pick the one that matched what you were doing. That is a curation problem, not a licensing budget problem, and a hundred station soundtrack does not solve it.

posts.author: mapnerd_leonida
posts.title: What we actually know about the map, written plainly for new people
posts.body:
Everything below is from Rockstar or a sourced interview. Nothing here is inference.

The game is set in the state of Leonida, based on Florida. There are six named regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park.

Vice City is the main city and contains named districts including Ocean Beach, Little Cuba, the Stockyard, Crosstown and the port. Grassrivers is wetland. Port Gellhorn is a run down coast. Ambrosia is inland industrial and agricultural. Mount Kalaga is northern wilderness on the state border. The Keys are an island chain.

Rockstar have said the whole map is around three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2's and that Vice City itself is roughly twice the size of Los Santos.

That is genuinely everything. Every layout diagram you have seen is a guess, including the good ones.

posts.author: keysrunner_88
posts.title: The good life is the phrase in both bios and nobody has pulled on it
posts.body:
Lucia wants the good life her mother has been dreaming of since Liberty City. Jason grew up around grifters and ended up working for drug runners, which is what happens to someone who never had a version of it to aim at.

Every GTA protagonist before this wanted something specific. Money, revenge, respect, out. This pair want a category. Not a house, not a number, just the good life, which is the vaguest possible ambition and the one most people actually have.

A story about two people who cannot articulate what they are working toward is a much harder thing to write than a story about a heist, and it is the only thing the marketing has consistently said.

posts.author: portgellhorn_
posts.title: Port Gellhorn is the only region named after a person and I have thoughts about it

Vice City, the Keys, Grassrivers, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga. Five names that describe a thing or sound like a place.

Gellhorn is a surname. Real American towns are named after people constantly, usually whoever owned the land or built the railway, and those names outlive any memory of the person. That is precisely the atmosphere the region description is going for: cheap motels, shut down attractions, a place that used to be for something.

A forgotten coast named after a forgotten person is the most economical piece of world building in the entire six region list, and it is doing that work before you have seen a single frame of it.

posts.author: portgellhorn_
posts.title: The actual historical gap between a Rockstar console launch and the PC version
posts.body:
Posting the pattern rather than a prediction, because the PC threads keep going in circles.

GTA V arrived on consoles in September 2013 and on PC in April 2015, which is about nineteen months, though that gap included a whole console generation transition in the middle.

Red Dead Redemption 2 was October 2018 on consoles and November 2019 on PC, which is thirteen months.

So the honest range from their own history is roughly twelve to twenty months, with nothing announced for this one. Anyone quoting a specific date is inventing it. Anyone saying never is ignoring two very clear precedents.

posts.title: What actually happens on launch day, hour by hour

For anyone who has not been through one of these, here is the realistic shape of November 19.

If you preloaded on the 12th, the game is already on your console as an encrypted blob you cannot open. At unlock it becomes playable, usually at local midnight though Rockstar has not confirmed the hour.

There will be a day one patch. It will be large. It downloads on top of the preload, so budget time and space for it.

The first hour will have store and licence check problems because everyone in your region is doing the same thing at the same time. This resolves itself. It is not your console.

Then you play, and the internet becomes unusable for a fortnight.

posts.author: portgellhorn_
posts.title: In defence of driving for eleven minutes and doing nothing
posts.body:
The complaint about big maps is always that there is nothing to do out there. I want to argue that nothing to do out there is the feature.

The reason Blaine County worked, and the reason the northern snow in Red Dead worked, is that they were places where the game stopped asking you for things. No markers, no calls, no reason to be there. That is not empty content, it is the absence of demand, and it is the only time these games let you just exist in the world they built.

A state that is three times the size of Red Dead's map with six named regions is going to have a lot of that, and a lot of people are going to file it under filler. It is the opposite of filler. It is the part you will remember in four years.

posts.author: mapnerd_leonida
posts.title: A short note on why every fan map is wrong in the same direction
posts.body:
Having looked at about a dozen of these now, they all make the same error and it is a psychological one rather than a geographic one.

Everyone draws the city in the middle. Every single map has Vice City roughly central with the five other regions arranged around it like petals.

There is no reason for that. Real states have their major city on a coast, usually offset badly, with enormous distances on one side and almost nothing on the other. Los Santos was in the south of its map. The city being central is not an inference from evidence, it is a habit from looking at maps where the important thing is in the middle because the person drawing it put it there.

posts.author: portgellhorn_
posts.title: The county names are doing more work than the region names
posts.body:
Vice-Dale County and Kelly County are the two that have appeared on signage.

Region names are chosen to sound evocative in marketing. County names are chosen to sound like they were assigned by a clerk in 1912 and never revisited. Vice-Dale is a hyphenated compound that only exists because two smaller places got merged and neither would give up its name, which is exactly how real county names happen.

That single hyphen implies a history nobody will ever explain, and it does more for making that state feel real than any amount of skyline.

So either faction systems are being held back entirely, or this game is structured around people rather than organisations. The second would be a real departure.

posts.author: jasonduvalfan
posts.title: Rereading Jason's bio for what is probably the fortieth time

Grew up around grifters and crooks. Ended up working for drug runners in the Keys. Meeting Lucia may be the best or the worst thing that ever happened to him.

What gets me now is the word ended up. Not chose, not turned to, not became. Ended up. Passive construction in a two sentence biography, and it is the only verb in there describing something he did.

That is the whole character. A man things happen to, meeting a woman who makes things happen.

posts.author: threehundredhours
posts.title: How long before somebody posts a hundred percent run

For the newcomers: those guides are the single fastest way to spoil a game for yourself, and they will be at the top of every search result by November 21.

posts.author: keysrunner_88

posts.author: preloadwatch
posts.title: How do timezone unlocks actually work

Rockstar has not said which this is. Both consoles support both models. Anyone know what they did for previous launches, and does anyone actually know how to tell in advance?

posts.author: vicebeachcam
posts.title: Will licensed music get clips muted
posts.body:
Practical question that will affect a lot of people here.

A game with a licensed soundtrack this large has a real problem with clip sharing, because platform copyright systems do not distinguish between a song in a game and a song in a video. Previous large releases have shipped a setting that disables licensed music specifically for capture.

Nothing has been said about whether this game has one. Given how much of the atmosphere is radio, it would be a strange omission and an even stranger thing to have to use.

Snapmatic returns, which is the in world camera. What I have not seen addressed is whether there is a separate photo mode with a free camera, exposure control, depth of field and the rest.

posts.author: portgellhorn_
posts.title: The regions I expect to be argued about most after launch
posts.body:
Writing this down now so it can be checked later.

Vice City will be praised and then criticised for being too dense to drive in. Grassrivers will be the one everyone posts screenshots of in week one and never returns to. Mount Kalaga will be called empty by people who spent forty minutes in it and beloved by people who spent forty hours.

Port Gellhorn will be dismissed in every review and will be somebody's favourite place in the game. Ambrosia will be the one nobody mentions at all, which is the worst outcome and the most likely one.

The Keys will be the surprise. I have no evidence for that. I just think a region built around water in a series that has never taken water seriously is where the actual novelty is hiding.

posts.author: nospoilersplease
posts.title: What is the plan for clip and screenshot etiquette in here after launch
posts.body:
Asking now rather than on November 20, because the moment it is out this becomes an argument instead of a discussion.

My suggestion is simple: story content behind a tag for the first month, everything else open. A screenshot of a beach is not a spoiler. A screenshot of a cutscene is.

I am aware I am the person who always raises this and that I have no authority to decide anything. Genuinely asking what people think is workable, because a rule nobody agrees with is worse than no rule.

posts.author: keysrunner_88
posts.title: Print Works, Love Fist, and the missions I still think about twenty four years later
posts.body:
Not a nostalgia dump, a question about what makes a mission stick.

The Print Works was mandatory to finish the game and it was also just a building you bought that made money. I remember it because it was mine.

The Love Fist missions were a rock band being idiots and me driving them around. I remember them because they were funny and because nothing else in the game was quite like them.

Neither is a spectacle. Neither has a set piece. What they have is ownership in one case and character in the other, and I would bet a lot that the missions people remember from this one in 2050 are the same two categories rather than whatever the biggest explosion is.

posts.author: portgellhorn_
posts.title: A newcomer's guide to which region to actually be excited about
posts.body:
Written for the people who have joined recently and are getting six region names thrown at them with no context.

Vice City is the city. It is what the game is called and it is where most of the story is. You will spend a lot of time here and it will be extremely good.

The other five are why the map is interesting. Grassrivers is wetland you cross by boat. Port Gellhorn is a run down coast. Ambrosia is farmland and industry. Mount Kalaga is wilderness. The Keys are islands.

Do not let anyone tell you which one to care about, including me, and I have opinions. The one you end up loving will be the one you find yourself in at two in the morning with no mission active.

posts.author: nospoilersplease
posts.title: The thing nobody tells newcomers about launch week
posts.body:
Everyone gives you advice about spoilers and storage and preloads. Here is the one nobody says.

You will not enjoy the first two hours as much as you expect to. Not because the game is bad. Because you have been waiting three years and no opening sequence survives that. You will be checking it against something in your head rather than playing it.

That feeling goes away somewhere around hour four, when you stop watching the game and start being in it. If you know it is coming it does not bother you. If you do not, you spend the first evening quietly worried that you have been let down.

Every single big release does this and it has nothing to do with the game.

posts.author: nospoilersplease
posts.title: My final answer on going dark, after a year of getting it wrong
posts.body:
This is the last time I post about this, I promise.

What I got wrong all year: I thought avoidance was a filtering problem. It is a surface area problem. Every improvement I made came from being in fewer places, not from being better at screening the places I was in.

What actually works, in order of effect: watching official material on Rockstar's own site rather than the video platform, because there is no recommendation wall. Unsubscribing rather than muting. Leaving two platforms entirely. Telling three colleagues in advance. Going off this forum from the 18th.

What does not work: muted words, filters, willpower, and telling yourself you will just look at one thread.

posts.author: holdmybeerpc
posts.title: Right, the actual criticisms, because somebody has to and it is obviously going to be me
posts.body:
Everything since Thursday has been superlatives. Here is the honest list of things that could still go wrong, from someone who thinks it will be excellent.

The systems shown are all inputs to other systems. Witness reports feed descriptions, descriptions feed pursuit, the profile feeds the world, money gates progress. That is elegant on paper and it means one badly tuned number makes four things feel bad at once.

Eighty hours of a story about two people needs those two people to carry eighty hours. RDR2 had a gang to spread that load across. This has a couple and a supporting cast we have not met.

And nobody has seen the top of the wanted system, the ending, two entire regions, or a single announced character in gameplay. We have been shown a very confident forty minutes about a game we have not actually seen the shape of.

Still preordering. Still annoyed about the PC thing lol

posts.author: oceandr1986
posts.title: The silence in that car conversation, one more time and then I will stop
posts.body:
I have written about this twice and I want to be specific about the thing rather than the feeling.

One of them says something. The other does not answer immediately. The car keeps going. The radio is low. Nothing on screen changes and nothing is signposted.

In a game, a pause costs money. Somebody has to animate the non response, hold the camera, resist filling it, and trust that the player will not think the audio has broken. Every instinct in game development says put a line there.

They did not. That is the whole reason I think this is going to be different from the last one.

posts.author: mapnerd_leonida
posts.title: The map post, final pre launch version
posts.body:
Co-signed by several people in the thread where I proposed it. This is what is actually known.

Setting: the state of Leonida, based on Florida.

Six named regions: Vice City, Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park.

Named districts of Vice City: Ocean Beach, Little Cuba, the Stockyard, Crosstown, the VC Port. Named counties: Vice-Dale, Kelly.

Size: roughly three times Red Dead Redemption 2's map, with Vice City about twice Los Santos. Both figures come from one interview with one Rockstar developer, and neither has been independently confirmed.

Shown in footage: Vice City extensively, Grassrivers clearly, and a run down coastal area that is almost certainly Port Gellhorn. Not shown at all: the Keys, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga.

Not known: layout, adjacency, travel times, the road network, or whether the wetland is traversable by car.

Every map diagram you have seen fills in that last paragraph with guesses. Some of the guesses are good. None of them is evidence.

September has the reveal still echoing. November has the game. October has nothing, and that is the problem.

I have watched myself do exactly this before two previous launches. The danger is not the week of release. The danger is the quiet month when you are bored and the game is close enough to feel real.

2. The quiet. Somebody in here posted about a residential street with an air conditioning unit and I have not stopped thinking about it since.
3. The pause in the car conversation. Four seconds. Three separate people have written about it better than I could.
4. Money mattering. V's economy was broken by hour twenty and stayed broken for a decade.

posts.author: mapnerd_leonida
posts.title: Survey method, first draft, for October
posts.body:
Since a few people said they would contribute, here is a draft method to argue about now rather than in November.

Distances measured by driving, not by map. Same vehicle for every run, chosen once and agreed. Timed from full stop to full stop. Three runs per route, median taken, all three published.

Routes defined between named locations only, never between coordinates, so anybody can reproduce them.

Water routes measured separately and never compared to road routes.

Everything published including the failures. If a route cannot be driven, that is a finding.

Argue with this now. The one thing I have learned from two months of scale threads is that nobody accepts a standard after they already have numbers they like.

posts.author: nospoilersplease
posts.title: The final newcomer post: everything you need and nothing you do not
posts.body:
Last one from me. If you have just joined, this is the whole thing.

The game is out November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series consoles. It costs 79.99 standard or 99.99 for the Ultimate edition, which adds cosmetics, some vehicles and five businesses with side missions. You can upgrade later, so buy standard.

Preorder before November 20 for the Vintage pack. Preload opens November 12. Clear 150 to 200 gigabytes before then, not on the day.

You do not need to have played any previous game. Nothing carries over and no story requires them.

That is everything you have to know. Two posts in this group cover the rest better than I could: the wanted level explainer and the map post. Everything else on this forum, mine especially, is people enjoying themselves.

Go in as clean as you can manage. It only happens once.

posts.author: preloadwatch
posts.title: Final checklist, seventy six days out
posts.body:
Consolidating everything from a year of these threads into one post so nobody has to search.

Before November 12: decide your edition, preorder if you want the Vintage pack, clear your storage, buy any expansion card now rather than in the rush.

November 12: preload opens. Physical copies ship, and they are a code in a box, not a disc.

November 18: nothing left to do. Charge your controllers, do your shopping, sleep.

November 19: unlock hour unconfirmed, probably local midnight. There will be a large day one patch on top of the preload, so leave headroom. The game needs one licence check even for single player, so be online once. If it fails, wait an hour. Do not reinstall anything.

That is the complete list. There is nothing else. I have been looking for something else to organise for three weeks and there is nothing.

posts.author: firstgtafr

Since then this place has taught me what a wanted level is, what a criminal profile might be, why the map arguments matter, how to clear storage, what to do if the licence check fails, and not to open a completion guide in November.

I have also read about a bakery, a crane, a hotel sign, thirty four fake brands, a fence in a field, and four seconds of two people not talking in a car.

I have not played a single Grand Theft Auto game. I will have played one in seventy six days. Thank you for being extremely patient with someone who did not know anything.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body:
Single player does not need servers to play, but on both consoles the game still has to check your licence once, and that check is what falls over on a launch day this size.

Practical version: preload from November 12, be online once on the 19th to let it verify, and after that you are fine. If the check fails, it is usually the storefront under load rather than the game, and it clears within a few hours.

replies.body: bikers next to a sugar refinery in the middle of nowhere. they do not need a name, i already know exactly what those people are like

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Every named faction in previous games arrived with a colour and a territory. If those exist here they have not been shown.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body:
My line is: anything Rockstar has shown is fair game, anything from a leak is not, and anything about the second half of the story is not regardless of source.

The reason I use source rather than content as the test is that content lines are arbitrary and source lines are not. Either Rockstar published it or somebody took it.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Source rather than content is a much cleaner rule than the one I have been using and I am adopting it.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: Mechanics are not spoilers. Learning that cars have alarms does not diminish anything. Learning who dies does. That is where I draw it.

replies.author: gatorinthepool
replies.body: a location is only a spoiler if the location itself is the surprise, which happens about twice per rockstar game and you never know which twice in advance

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: That last point is the honest problem with my whole position and I do not have an answer to it.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: The line definitely moves after launch. Two weeks in, the burden shifts to the person who has not played it yet, and I think that is correct.

replies.author: kalaga_hiker
replies.body: Two weeks feels short. RDR2 took me four months and I was not being slow on purpose.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body:
Nothing beyond the plays best line, which is marketing copy rather than a specification. No frame rate target has been given for any platform.

Worth noting they have never published performance targets before a launch. RDR2's console modes were only detailed in reviews. This silence is normal for them even if it is unusual for the industry.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: That context helps a lot. I had assumed the silence was unusual and it turns out the industry changed around them.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: Expect a performance mode and a fidelity mode because every game does now. Expect no announcement until the embargo lifts.

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: Which will be about four days before launch and by then everyone will have preordered, which is the actual reason for the silence.

replies.author: tulipdriver
replies.body: Being cynical about it and being right about it are not mutually exclusive here.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: You are right and I think the reason is structural. RDR2 could tell you the gang was falling apart because that is the premise, not the plot. Here the premise may be the plot, in which case they cannot say it.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Three years of marketing that establishes character and place and says nothing about story is a deliberate strategy and an unusually confident one.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: Or the honest possibility: the story changed during development and the marketing was built around the parts that were fixed. That happens more than anyone admits.

replies.author: lucia_did_nothing
replies.body: thats fair and i dont think it excludes my read. the parts that were fixed being who they are and where they are is still a choice about what to lead with

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: Speaking as the resident spoiler avoider, a marketing campaign that tells me nothing about the story is the best possible outcome and I have not seen one in years.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: Two delays also means the marketing had to survive eighteen months longer than planned, which argues for keeping it non specific.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Nothing states the employment relationship. What exists is that Jason works around drug runners in the Keys, that Heder is a Keys figure, and that Cal is described as an associate of Heder. Boss is an inference and a reasonable one.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: The Cal connection is the one that makes boss feel too simple. If Cal is an associate of Heder and a friend of Jason, then Heder is the hub of that whole social group rather than an employer sitting above it.

replies.author: jasonduvalfan
replies.body: That is a much better model and it changes how I read Jason. He is not working for someone, he is inside something.

replies.author: lucia_did_nothing
replies.body: inside something is way worse than working for someone. you can quit a job

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: And that is the whole reason meeting Lucia could be the best or the worst thing that happened to him.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Cruise ship capital of the world is doing specific work. Container ports are geometry. Cruise terminals are crowds, which is expensive, and you do not spend that on a backdrop.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: That was my instinct and I wanted a second opinion before saying it. A cruise terminal is a pedestrian space full of tourists, which is a completely different design problem to a dock.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: A ship the size of a building that you can be on is one of the things this series has never done and the port description makes it sound possible.

replies.author: gatorinthepool
replies.body: cruise ships are the single most florida form of transport and putting them in the same game as a kayak is very funny to me

replies.author: tulipdriver
replies.body: Ports in these games have historically been where the good vehicles spawn and where the police response is worst. Both things at once.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: Demonstrating rather than asserting is the right framing. Six hundred thousand animations is a number that is only impressive because it is a number nobody would bother to fake.

replies.author: tulipdriver
replies.body: Fifty commissioned muralists is the detail that convinced me. That is a procurement problem, a legal problem and a scheduling problem, and no one takes it on for a press line.

replies.author: lucia_did_nothing
replies.body: hiring fifty artists to paint walls in a video game is insane behaviour and i mean that as the highest compliment available

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: The statement will age either very well or very badly depending on what the next game does, and they must know that.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: Saying it out loud creates an obligation. That is the actual significance and it is why most publishers have avoided saying anything.

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: It does not make the game better on its own is the necessary caveat and I appreciate you including it rather than letting the thread become a moral one.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body:
Snapmatic is the in game camera and photo system from previous games. It is a phone app you use to frame and take photos, and in past titles you could share them.

You do not need to understand anything before launch. It is a phone app and the game will hand it to you. The detail people are excited about is that the protagonists apparently avoid posting theirs publicly, which is a story detail rather than something you need to manage.

replies.author: rydeme_driver
replies.body: That is exactly what I needed, thank you. I had built it up into something I would have to learn.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: Worth knowing that in previous games the photo system turned into a whole hobby for a section of the community. You can ignore it entirely or lose fifty hours to it.

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: And a warning for the newcomers group specifically: photo mode communities are where launch week spoilers travel fastest.

replies.author: dade_county_jay
replies.body: i took like 400 photos in rdr2 and looked at none of them again. still worth it

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body:
V's main story was somewhere around thirty hours for me without chasing anything. RDR2 was closer to fifty five and I was not being thorough.

So the eighty figure, if it is comparable, is either a substantially longer story or the same length story plus meaningful optional content. Both are plausible and the quoted number does not distinguish between them.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: Thirty for V matches mine almost exactly. RDR2 took me over sixty and I skipped things.

replies.author: gatorinthepool
replies.body: rdr2 took me a hundred and forty hours and i did not finish the story. i was fishing. this is not useful data for anyone

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: It is actually the most useful data in the thread because it is what happens to most people.

replies.author: tulipdriver
replies.body: Thirty five for V. The range in this thread is thirty to sixty for a main story, which is a good honest bracket to give newcomers.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: Thirty to sixty depending entirely on whether you are the kind of person who stops to look at things. That is the real answer and it is not about the game at all.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: Agreed and I would go further. For a first GTA the extras are actively unhelpful, because cosmetic unlocks and extra businesses give you options before you understand what any of the options mean.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: Buy Standard, and if you are still playing in December buy the upgrade then. The upgrade path exists precisely so nobody has to decide now.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: The counterargument, weakly: preordering either edition gets you the Vintage pack, so if you want that you have to decide before launch. But that is about preordering, not about which edition.

replies.author: bought_ultimate
replies.body: Right, and that is a fair distinction. Vintage pack is a preorder question. Ultimate is not, and people keep merging them.

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: Good thread for the newcomers group. This is the only decision anybody has to make before November and it is smaller than it looks.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Nothing. I went through it frame by frame for exactly this and there is no platform information beyond the two console families, no small print, and no mention of any performance option.

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: Confirming the same. The end card is the two consoles and the date. That is the entire technical content of forty minutes.

replies.author: holdmybeerpc

replies.author: keysrunner_88

replies.author: oceandr1986

replies.author: justhereforonline

replies.author: keysrunner_88

replies.author: sixstarsplz
replies.body: and it ties straight into the report thing. take longer, more people see you, more chance someone calls it in. every system in this game is talking to every other one

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body: Damaging the contents by blowing it fast is the elegant part. The cost is not abstract risk, it is a smaller number in your hands afterwards.

replies.author: holdmybeerpc

replies.author: threehundredhours

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body:
Fourteen tracks across five decades, ranging from eighties rock and synth pop through country to contemporary rap. Someone will have a complete list up within a day.

On your second question: trailer music has occasionally overlapped with in game radio in past titles but it is not a rule, and licensing for the two is negotiated separately. Overlap is possible, not implied.

replies.author: oceandr1986
replies.body: Five decades explains why I could place half of it and not the rest... some of that is genuinely older than the setting.

replies.author: tommysshirt

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: That effect is almost certainly deliberate. Using period music over a modern setting is how you tell a returning player that this is the same city and not the same time.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: Country in the mix is the one people are skipping over and it is the strongest hint that there is a whole region up north that we have barely seen.

replies.author: lucia_did_nothing
replies.body: its rdr2 shaped. funny world, sad people. v was the other way round, sad world funny people

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: That is the cleanest formulation of it I have read. The satire is aimed outward at the world and the characters are being treated seriously, which is a reversal for this series.

replies.author: portgellhorn_
replies.body: V's problem was that it could not decide whether to care about its characters. If this one has decided, that is the biggest improvement available to them.

replies.author: jasonduvalfan
replies.body: The fake adverts are broad and the two leads are not. Those can coexist because the ads are the world talking and the characters are people living in it.

replies.author: oceandr1986
replies.body: Funny world, sad people. I am going to be thinking about that phrasing until November.

replies.author: nospoilersplease
replies.body: The colder stretches are what convinced me this is not going to be V with better lighting.

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body:
Focus is described as highlighting useful objects or opportunities. Whether it is held, toggled or contextual has not been shown, and the three descriptions you have read are three people guessing at that gap.

Greet and taunt are separate. Those are the NPC interaction options that appear when your weapon is holstered, with defuse and provoke appearing in tense situations instead.

replies.author: quietcal
replies.body: Separate systems then. That is the bit everyone is merging and it is why the descriptions all differ.

replies.author: sixstarsplz
replies.body: defuse and provoke only showing up when things are already tense is such a good detail. the game knows what kind of moment youre in

replies.author: keysrunner_88

replies.author: lucia_did_nothing
replies.body: npcs confronting you for following them too long is the detail that got me. theyre paying attention back

replies.author: neonlightsvc

replies.author: keysrunner_88

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: The RDR2 camp comparison has been made a lot this week and this is the first time someone has said what it actually means rather than just naming it.

replies.author: oceandr1986
replies.body: Shaving your own head badly instead of going to a barber is such a specific piece of design... someone fought for that.

replies.author: threehundredhours

replies.author: mapnerd_leonida

replies.author: vicebeachcam
replies.body:
A mask removes one line from the description rather than granting immunity. The system builds a description out of appearance, clothing and vehicle, so covering your face leaves the other two intact.

That is why changing clothes and switching vehicles are both mentioned alongside masks. It is a set of attributes and you are trying to break enough of them.

replies.author: sixstarsplz
replies.body: ok that makes so much more sense than how i was thinking about it. its not a disguise its a checklist you are trying to fail

replies.author: quietcal
replies.body: A checklist you are trying to fail is a genuinely great way to describe it and I am stealing that.

replies.author: holdmybeerpc
replies.body: The gap between how people say they will play and how they actually play is where this system gets interesting lol

replies.author: vicebeachcam

replies.body: ok this thread has made me significantly more excited about a name i could not even source

replies.author: mapnerd_leonida

replies.author: preloadwatch
replies.body: Which means every scale estimate posted this week is based on the interview quote and nothing else. The footage added zero.

replies.author: holdmybeerpc
replies.body: Zero usable scale data in forty minutes of gameplay is genuinely impressive editing discipline when you think about it lol

replies.author: gatorinthepool

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body: Leonida is not a one to one Florida in any case. The regions are composites and the geography is compressed, which is what they did with San Andreas and with the RDR2 map.

replies.author: keysrunner_88
replies.body:
Short version. Commit a crime, the police become interested, and the level of interest is shown as stars. More stars means more police, better equipped, more persistent. You escape by getting away and staying unseen until they lose interest.

The change this time is that the police have to find out first, and what they find out becomes a description of you. That is the part that is new.
